_comment: ESM-2 fine-tuning. The familiar LLM setup -- this is the one lab in the section where nothing about the config is unusual.
_batch_comment: train_batch_size is DELIBERATELY OMITTED so DeepSpeed derives it as micro x accum x num_gpus and any --num_gpus works without editing this file. The unit here is a CHAIN (one protein with its MSA), not a token: micro=2 means two proteins per rank per step. Two is small on purpose -- the activation cost scales with N_res^3, so batch size is the cheapest knob to turn when a longer protein will not fit.
_precision_comment: bf16 ON, unlike 04_structure_module which disables it. There is no precision-sensitive measurement here; this is ordinary transformer fine-tuning and bf16 roughly halves activation memory, which is what lets 650M fit a 24 GB card alongside LoRA. Needs Ampere or newer; on Volta/Turing use fp16, never both.
_zero_comment: Stage 2 -- and here the ordinary reasoning APPLIES, which it did not in the other three folders. ESM-2 650M has 652M real parameters, so optimizer state and gradients are gigabytes and sharding them is worth real memory. Compare 02_evoformer, where the model is 100k parameters and the stage is nearly irrelevant: same course, same knob, opposite conclusion, because the memory is in a different place.
_bucket_comment: reduce_bucket_size is set EXPLICITLY, and that matters more than it looks. Leave it out and DeepSpeed defaults it to 5e8 -- a 500 MB reduction buffer -- while ds_config_z3.json sets 16 MB. The first version of these two files differed in exactly that way, so the ZeRO-1-vs-ZeRO-3 comparison this lab invites read 1.58 GB vs 0.62 GB and appeared to show stage 3 winning by 2.5x. It was measuring the buckets, not the stage. These two configs are now identical except for the stage, which is the only way the comparison means anything.
_checkpointing_comment: Activation checkpointing is configured but left OFF by default so the baseline measurement is honest. Turn it on with --activation-checkpointing to recompute the triangle activations in the backward pass instead of storing them: real memory relief, at roughly 30% more compute. Unlike the ZeRO stage, this one attacks the tensor that is actually large.
